atomicity.reason: One reaction, but two independently violable limit conditions (below pack.cell_v_min, above pack.cell_v_max) that the supervisor's limit table lists as separate limits (undervoltage, overvoltage); either clause alone would stand as a complete requirement.
atomicity.suggestion: Split into an undervoltage and an overvoltage requirement, or keep the window as one deliberate unit and say so explicitly.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained: the title states the limits are the chemistry's safe window and the variant roles name them unambiguously.

feasibility.reason: A per-cell window comparison on the 10 ms cycle is standard BMS practice and consistent with the latch, reaction-time and record requirements.

parent_fit.reason: Directly implements 'any cell leaves its safe voltage window' from US_CELL_PROTECTION: per-cell evaluation, one cell outside the window is sufficient, contactors commanded open.

unambiguity.reason: Single reading: a valid reading of any one cell strictly below the minimum or strictly above the maximum triggers the reaction, independent of pack voltage.

verifiability.reason: Both bounds are explicit parameters in V (variant roles pack.cell_v_min and pack.cell_v_max), comparisons are strict and scope is per cell, so pass/fail is exact for a given variant; 'valid' is defined by REQ_MEASUREMENT_PLAUSIBILITY and timing by REQ_FAULT_REACTION_TIME. The resolved numbers are not visible in the audit view, so they are assumed to be defined per variant.

summary: Well-parented, testable per-cell voltage window with variant-bound limits; it bundles undervoltage and overvoltage into a single requirement.
